contexts.text: Cities sown with salt. Explained. AC 2455:end.
They who sow beside all waters () = those who suffer themselves to be instructed in spiritual things.
To sow wheat () = the goods which are of love and charity.
A land not sown () = defect of truths.
Neither ploughed nor sown () = not cultivated with the truths and goods of faith, on account of ignorance.
Six years thou shalt sow the land () = the first state, when the man of the Church is being instructed in the truths and goods of faith. Explained.
That to sow the land, or a field, = to teach and learn the truths and goods of faith which are of the Church. Illustrated.
Not to sow the land (in the seventh year) () = not to be led by means of truths, as before.
To plough and sow = to learn.
To sow the fields () = to be instructed, and to receive truths.
It is not sown () = no receptibility of the truth of the Church.
To sow and reap = the implantation of good and its reception.
